code_assets.name: safe-redirect.ts — open-redirect guards
code_assets.summary: Collapses any user-supplied redirect to a same-origin path and restricts callback URLs to loopback.
code_assets.description: Security helper added for potpie-ai/potpie#596. `getSafeInternalPath(raw, fallback)` decodes once (`decodeOnce`), then rejects anything that is not a rooted same-origin path — absolute URLs, protocol-relative `//host`, backslash tricks such as `/\evil.com`, and control characters — and finally resolves the value against a `https://internal.invalid` sentinel origin to confirm it stayed there. `isLoopbackCallbackUrl` accepts only http(s) loopback targets such as `http://localhost:54333/auth/callback`, which is what stops a hostile `redirect_uri` from exfiltrating a Firebase token. Grep here for open redirect handling or when a legitimate redirect target is silently dropped.

code_assets.name: vscode-callback.ts — VS Code auth callback URL builder
code_assets.summary: Builds the loopback callback URL that carries the Firebase ID token and custom token back to the extension.
code_assets.description: Exports `buildVSCodeCallbackUrl(token, customToken?, redirectUri?)`. Both tokens are appended through `URLSearchParams` so they are percent-encoded; the extension must read `token` and `customToken` from the decoded query and tolerate a long (>2KB) query string. Grep here when the VS Code sign-in callback 404s, uses the wrong port, or truncates a JWT.

code_assets.description: Pre-commit configuration for the potpie repo. pre-commit-hooks v5.0.0 supplies check-yaml (`--unsafe`), check-toml, check-json, check-ast, trailing-whitespace, end-of-file-fixer, mixed-line-ending, check-merge-conflict, check-case-conflict, a 25 MB large-file cap, detect-private-key and debug-statements. ruff-pre-commit v0.14.3 runs `ruff` with an `--extend-ignore` list (E402, S101, S105, S106, S110, S311, S324, S603, S607, S608, E722) and `ruff-format`, both excluding `^legacy/`. uv-pre-commit 0.10.7 runs `uv-lock --check` so a stale lockfile blocks the commit, and a local hook runs `cargo fmt` over `potpie/parsing/*.rs`. code_assets.name: cli-flow.md — the potpie CLI command reference
code_assets.summary: The canonical grouped reference for every potpie command, its flags, and the shared CLI plumbing.
code_assets.description: Repo-root documentation describing the full `potpie` CLI surface (status line: reflects code on main @ 49e12528). It establishes that there is no separate human-vs-agent API — people and coding harnesses drive the same CLI, with agents optionally reaching the same internals through the four in-process MCP `context_*` tools — that `potpie/cli/main.py build_app()` is the single Typer console entrypoint declared in `[project.scripts]`, and that every command routes `CLI → HostShell → service(s) → ports`. Documents the root `@app.callback` global options (`--json`, `--verbose`/`-v`, `--version`) and the shared `commands/_common.py` plumbing: `get_host()` returning a daemon-backed `RemoteHostShell` by default, `contract()` and `resolve_pot_id`. Grep here for a command's flags or the canonical first-run journey.

code_assets.name: legacy/pyproject.toml — optional legacy demo host manifest
code_assets.summary: Setuptools manifest for `potpie-legacy`, the deletable FastAPI/Celery demo host.
code_assets.description: Project file for the `potpie-legacy` distribution, whose own description reads 'Optional Potpie demo host (FastAPI, agents, Celery, seed). Delete this folder if you only need core packages.' It depends on `potpie-context-core`, `potpie-context-engine[all]` and `potpie-integrations` alongside the old server stack (alembic, anthropic, aiohttp and the rest), and is built with setuptools rather than the hatchling used by the modern packages. `.pre-commit-config.yaml` excludes `^legacy/` from ruff and ruff-format, which is why lint sweeps over the shipped packages never touch it. Grep here when deciding whether a dependency belongs to the shipped CLI or only to the deprecated server.

code_assets.name: read_presenter.py — human rendering for graph read and timeline
code_assets.summary: Turns read results into bullets or tables for `potpie graph read` and `potpie timeline recent`.
code_assets.description: The presentation layer for the CLI's read commands, kept deliberately out of the services. `build_presentation_context` assembles a frozen `ReadPresentationContext` (view, detail, relations, format mode, sort, dedupe), then `render_timeline_events`, `render_timeline_table`, `render_items_bullets` and `render_items_table` emit the human output, with helpers for relation display (`_relations_cell`, `_format_relations_summary`, `_format_relations_full_lines`, `_related_keys_from_relations`), fact truncation at `_FACT_TRUNCATE_LEN = 120` and a `_DEFAULT_ITEM_LIMIT` of 10. Normalisation comes from `potpie_context_core.ports.graph_service`. Grep here when `graph read` output is formatted wrong — never when the underlying data is wrong.

code_assets.name: errors.py — the domain error hierarchy
code_assets.summary: Every context-engine domain exception, translated to HTTP or CLI codes only at adapter boundaries.
code_assets.description: Defines `ContextEngineError` and its subclasses: `ContextEngineDisabled` (feature flag off or graph clients unavailable), `AlreadyIngested` (source already in the ingestion ledger), `UpstreamError` (GitHub, Neo4j or Postgres failed), `BridgeError`, `PotNotFound`, `MutationBatchValidationError`, `ReconciliationApplyError` and `CapabilityNotImplemented` — the last being what an unbuilt seam raises so `potpie setup` reports `not_implemented` instead of crashing. Domain code raises these; only adapters map them onto exit codes and HTTP statuses. Grep here to trace an error message back to the layer that raises it, or to add a new failure mode.

code_assets.name: graph_entity_summary.py — entity display-property normalization
code_assets.summary: Guarantees every entity carries a non-empty name, summary and description within a character budget.
code_assets.description: Small helper module behind the retrieval-card contract. `compact_entity_summary(*candidates, max_chars=MAX_ENTITY_SUMMARY_CHARS)` returns the first non-empty candidate, cleaned by `_clean_text` and truncated by `_truncate` to the 320-character `MAX_ENTITY_SUMMARY_CHARS` budget. `normalize_entity_properties(properties, entity_key=...)` fills in a missing name, summary or description on a property bag, and `merge_entity_display_properties` folds incoming display properties over existing ones without blanking good text. Grep here for blank entity summaries in read output, or for where truncation ellipses come from.

code_assets.name: graph_plans.py — mutation-plan DTOs for propose then commit
code_assets.summary: The persisted plan record, diff, approval and commit-result types that make `graph commit <plan_id>` payload-free.
code_assets.description: Graph V2 plan serialization. Defines `GraphMutationPlanStatus`, `GraphMutationDiff`, `GraphMutationApproval`, `GraphMutationPlanRecord`, `GraphMutationProposal`, `GraphIngestionVerificationResult` and `GraphMutationCommitResult`, plus round-trip helpers `mutation_batch_to_dict`/`mutation_batch_from_dict`, `provenance_context_to_dict`/`provenance_context_from_dict` and `event_ref_to_dict`/`event_ref_from_dict`. Because the plan store persists a server-created, validated, already-lowered `MutationBatch`, the agent never resends the mutation payload at commit time — it commits a plan id. Grep here for plan status transitions, `_parse_datetime`/`_json_safe`, or 'plan not found' and 'plan expired' behaviour.

code_assets.name: graph_workbench.py — Graph V2 command envelope DTOs
code_assets.summary: The CLI workbench protocol: the command vocabulary and the outer envelope wrapping every V1.5 result.
code_assets.description: Declares the workbench contract that sits above the V1.5 data plane: `GRAPH_WORKBENCH_CONTRACT_VERSION = "v2"`, `GRAPH_WORKBENCH_ONTOLOGY_VERSION` (taken from `graph_contract.ONTOLOGY_VERSION`), the public `GRAPH_WORKBENCH_COMMANDS` tuple — status, catalog, describe, search-entities, read, neighborhood, propose, commit, bulk, history, inbox, quality — and `GRAPH_WORKBENCH_ADMIN_COMMANDS` (repair, export and friends). These are DTOs only; the envelope assembly logic lives in workbench_service.py, which was split out of the former `application/services/graph_workbench.py` when context-core was flattened. Grep here to add a workbench command or to check whether one is admin-gated.

code_assets.name: context-engine/pyproject.toml — the engine package manifest
code_assets.summary: Declares potpie-context-engine's deliberately thin base dependencies and its per-surface optional extras.
code_assets.description: Hatchling project file for `potpie-context-engine` 0.1.0 ('Context graph API, webhooks, daemon, and MCP'), built with the custom `distribution_defaults_hook.py` build hook. The base dependency set is only `potpie-context-core==0.1.0` and `pydantic>=2.0` — importing the package must not drag in a delivery surface or a storage backend. Everything else lives in `[project.optional-dependencies]`: `cli-auth` (httpx, keyring), `http` (fastapi, uvicorn, plus the `starlette>=1.3.1` CVE floor from #1015), `local` (falkordb, falkordblite for Python 3.12+, and a pinned redis because redis 8 maintenance notifications break FalkorDBLite) and an `all` roll-up. Grep here when an import fails because an extra is missing, or when a CVE floor needs bumping.

code_assets.name: api.py — the engine's stable public import surface
code_assets.summary: Re-exports GraphBackend and the store ports so consumers never import internal layer paths.
code_assets.description: A 30-line facade module: consumers composing a graph runtime write `from potpie_context_engine.api import GraphBackend, GraphInboxStorePort, GraphPlanStorePort, GraphService` instead of reaching into internal layers, so the package reorganisations of the three-way split do not break them. It re-exports those four names from `potpie_context_core.ports.*` and deliberately imports only stdlib-light domain contracts — no delivery adapters, no backend drivers — so importing it stays cheap and side-effect free. Grep here when deciding what is public API versus internal, or when an import of an internal path should be rewritten.

code_assets.name: daemon/main.py — the local daemon host process
code_assets.summary: The `potpie-daemon` entrypoint: a token-authenticated FastAPI RPC surface over the HostShell.
code_assets.description: Runnable host for the detached local daemon, exposed as the `potpie-daemon` console script. `create_app(token, base_url, pid, log_file)` builds a FastAPI app that authorizes every request against a shared secret (`_authorize`), dispatches RPC calls only to members of the `_ALLOWED_RPC_SURFACES` frozenset (`_validate_rpc_target`, `_resolve`), runs blocking host calls through `run_in_threadpool`, mounts the read-only local UI via `build_ui_api_router`/`mount_ui_static`, and writes the pid and discovery files that `start_detached` waits on. `main()` picks a free port with `_free_port` and serves under uvicorn. Grep here for 401s from the daemon, `_error_payload`, `_daemon_trace_id`, or an RPC surface that is refused.

code_assets.name: launcher.py — detached daemon start and stop
code_assets.summary: Starts the daemon as a background process and blocks until its discovery file appears, or stops it.
code_assets.description: The reliable start/stop mechanism behind the `potpie.daemon.daemon.Daemon` seam, moved here from context-engine's `adapters/outbound/daemon_process/` by the root-package migration. `start_detached(...)` spawns the daemon with `project_child_environment` derived from `RuntimeSettings`, blocks until readiness is signalled by the discovery file, returns the discovery metadata, and raises `DaemonStartError` on timeout — it is QUIET and never prints, so it is safe to call from inside a Rich live setup UI. `stop_daemon(home)` reads the pidfile via `read_pid_file` and signals the process. Grep here for DaemonStartError, a daemon that never comes up, or hangs during `potpie setup`.

code_assets.name: cli/telemetry/settings.py — telemetry resolution and status
code_assets.summary: Resolves whether telemetry is blocked, disabled or enabled and builds the Sentry and PostHog settings.
code_assets.description: Folds runtime settings and the user's stored preference into one answer for the CLI. Defines the `TelemetryState` literal ('blocked' | 'disabled' | 'enabled') and `TelemetrySinkStatus` ('anonymous' | 'blocked' | 'disabled'), plus the frozen dataclasses `TelemetryResolution`, `TelemetryStatus` and `ProductAnalyticsSettings`. `load_telemetry_resolution()`, `load_cli_runtime_settings()`, `load_sentry_settings()`, `load_product_analytics_settings()` and `load_telemetry_status()` are what `potpie telemetry` and the CLI bootstrap call, with `telemetry_enabled_by_preference` supplying the opt-out and `default_cli_release`/`telemetry_environment` stamping Sentry. Grep here when telemetry is unexpectedly on or off, or a Sentry release tag looks wrong.

code_assets.name: host_wiring.py — the composition root
code_assets.summary: `build_host_shell` wires every service and adapter behind the seams into a single HostShell.
code_assets.description: The one composition root for the agent surface (CLI plus MCP). `build_host_shell(...)` selects a backend profile through `default_backend_profile()` — default `falkordb_lite`, the embedded FalkorDBLite local stack needing no Docker, overridable with `$CONTEXT_ENGINE_BACKEND`, with `neo4j` as the shape-first production target — picks a host mode with `default_host_mode()`, and assembles the graph backend (`build_backend`), `LocalJsonGraphInboxStore`, `LocalJsonGraphPlanStore`, `LocalInstaller`, `LocalLedgerCursorStore` and the pot, skills and daemon services into a `HostShell`. The HTTP ingestion subsystem keeps its own root at `bootstrap/ingestion_server.py` and is not imported on the CLI path. Grep here to swap an adapter, add a service to the shell, or trace why a capability is unavailable.

code_assets.name: setup_orchestrator.py — the first-run setup sequence
code_assets.summary: One ordered seam plan drives preview, plan and run for `potpie setup`, folding each step into a SetupReport.
code_assets.description: `DefaultSetupOrchestrator` calls the bespoke per-component lifecycle methods in dependency order and folds each outcome into a `SetupReport`. Every step is wrapped so an unbuilt body raising `CapabilityNotImplemented` becomes a `not_implemented` `StepResult` and any other error becomes `failed` — setup runs what is ready and reports the rest rather than crashing. A single `_SEAM_PLAN` table is the source of truth for step order, owners and actions, and `preview` (dry-run), `plan` (deprecated alias) and `run` all derive from it. `_SOFT_STEPS` (auth, source, skills, embeddings.model) never gate `SetupReport.ok`, and `_HOST_GATED` steps (installer, daemon) are hard for a detached daemon and skipped for an in-process host — see `_is_hard`, `_skip_reason`, `_planned_steps`. Grep here for a setup step that is skipped, or for `_resolve_setup_repo_location` and `_current_git_remote`.

code_assets.name: falkordb_backend.py — the FalkorDB GraphBackend profile
code_assets.summary: Wraps the FalkorDB reader and writer behind the same capability bundle Neo4j uses, including Lite mode.
code_assets.description: Implements the `falkordb` and `falkordb_lite` backend profiles so application services see only `GraphBackend` and never a Falkor-specific graph handle. `FalkorDBGraphBackend` exposes `graph_writer`, `claim_query`, `mutation` (a `_FalkorDBMutation` with apply / invalidate / reset_pot / readiness over `apply_mutation_batch`), `semantic` (`ClaimQuerySemanticSearch`) and analytics (`ClaimQueryAnalytics`) capabilities, with `_FalkorDBModeSettings` selecting Lite versus server mode and `_run_sync` bridging async ports onto the synchronous driver. Unbuilt capabilities return `UnimplementedSnapshot`. Grep here for `_LITE_PROFILE`, `BackendReadiness`, or a 'backend not enabled' error on the default local profile.

code_assets.name: falkordb_reader.py — FalkorDB ClaimQueryPort
code_assets.summary: Read surface for the readers over FalkorDB, reusing the Neo4j Cypher and adding native vector recall.
code_assets.description: `FalkorDBClaimQueryStore` implements `ClaimQueryPort` at parity with `Neo4jClaimQueryStore`: the same canonical `:RELATES_TO` claim shape, the same filters and the same `ClaimRow` output. The Phase-0 spike proved the entire `_FIND_CLAIMS_CYPHER` (IN lists, IS NULL guards, temporal predicates, `labels()` filters) runs unchanged on FalkorDB, so this adapter reuses the Neo4j query constants and row parsers and only swaps the driver call plus record normalization — FalkorDB returns `result_set` rows rather than Neo4j `Record` maps. `fact_query` uses `_VECTOR_CLAIMS_CYPHER` against FalkorDB's native relationship vector index when an embedder is wired and falls back to `_find_claims_lexical` when the index or procedure is unavailable. Grep here for `_distance_to_similarity`, entity_properties, or semantic search silently returning lexical results.

code_assets.name: falkordb_writer.py — FalkorDB GraphWriterPort
code_assets.summary: The five write verbs on FalkorDB, reusing cypher.py through an async shim over the synchronous client.
code_assets.description: `FalkorDBGraphWriter` implements `GraphWriterPort` on the same Position-B substrate as the Neo4j writer, delegating the bitemporal and supersession mutation Cypher to `cypher.py` through `_FalkorAsyncDriver`, `_FalkorAsyncSession` and `_FalkorAsyncResult` — a thin async shim over the synchronous `falkordb` client — instead of duplicating that logic. Only three things are FalkorDB-specific: the shim; `ensure_indexes`, which uses the unnamed `CREATE INDEX FOR ... ON (...)` form best-effort via `_index_statements` because FalkorDB rejects named indexes and `IF NOT EXISTS`; and `reset_pot`, which deletes in client-side batches of `_RESET_BATCH = 500` scoped to `group_id` because FalkorDB has no `CALL {} IN TRANSACTIONS`. `build_falkordb_graph` and `FalkorDBGraphProvider` construct the handle; the default local mode is embedded FalkorDBLite over a local file. Grep here for index-creation failures or slow pot resets.

code_assets.name: local_pot_store.py — the local pot control plane
code_assets.summary: Flat JSON file at <home>/pots.json holding pots, sources, the active pot and repo-to-pot defaults.
code_assets.description: Backs `LocalPotManagementService` so pot state survives across CLI invocations, since every `potpie` call is a fresh process. `LocalPotStore` reads and writes `<home>/pots.json`, where `default_home()` resolves `$CONTEXT_ENGINE_HOME` or `~/.potpie`, and exposes `list_pots`, `active`, `create`, `use`, `rename`, `archive`, `add_source`, `list_sources`, `remove_source` plus repo routing (`repo_default`, `set_repo_default`, `clear_repo_default`, `list_repo_defaults`, `_repo_identity_key`, `_resolve_ref`). It is an explicit POC and carries a TODO to be replaced by the SQLite local state DB with migrations described in cli-flow.md. Grep here when the active pot resets, a registered source disappears, or repo-to-pot routing picks the wrong pot.

code_assets.name: readers/_common.py — shared reader scaffolding
code_assets.summary: ReadRequest and ReadResponse plus the scope, dedupe, coverage and ranking helpers every reader shares.
code_assets.description: The common substrate for the P9 use-case readers, so each reader holds only logic specific to itself. Defines `ReadRequest` and `ReadResponse`, `make_task_context`, `coverage_status_from_count`, `rank_candidates` (delegating scoring to `RankingService`), the claim helpers `claim_candidate_key`, `dedupe_claim_rows`, `_claim_row_dedupe_key`, `claim_corroboration`, `claim_semantic_similarity`, `claim_environment` and `claim_payload`, and the scope machinery `service_anchor_keys`, `scoped_entity_keys`, `row_in_anchor_set`, `graph_read_scope`, `scope_ref_matches` and `code_scope_conflicts`, alongside `_PATH_SCOPE_KEYS` and `QUERY_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD = 0.70`. Grep here when every reader's coverage or scope filtering changes at once.

code_assets.name: coding_preferences.py — the preferences reader (UC1)
code_assets.summary: Returns ranked coding preferences whose code_scope overlaps the current task scope.
code_assets.description: `CodingPreferencesReader.read(req)` queries claim edges with `predicate='POLICY_APPLIES_TO'` whose `code_scope` overlaps the task scope (language, framework, repo, service, file_path), optionally taking a semantic-similarity hop through the claim-query port's `fact_query` for fuzzy task phrasing, then ranks results with `RankingService` and surfaces the strength tier in each item's payload. Scope intersection is use-case-specific and lives here — `_normalise_scope_for_overlap`, `_scope_overlap`, `_scope_conflicts`, `_payload_from_row` — while ranking stays in P7, per the plan rule that no reader contains logic specific to another reader. Grep here when the preferences view returns the wrong rules for a file.

code_assets.name: readers/features.py — the features reader
code_assets.summary: Answers 'what does this repo or service provide?' from PROVIDES and IMPLEMENTED_IN claims only.
code_assets.description: `FeaturesReader.read(req)` deliberately reads only `PROVIDES` and `IMPLEMENTED_IN` claims so feature context is not polluted by generic topology edges. `_rows` fetches claims anchored on the scoped entity keys, `_feature_keys` collects the distinct feature entities, `_scope_overlap` scores anchor-set membership and `_payload_from_row` shapes each ranked item, with coverage reported through `coverage_status_from_count`. Grep here when the features view returns unrelated topology, or when a feature that was just written does not appear in `potpie graph read --subgraph features`.

code_assets.name: test_premerge_cli_journey.py — fresh-clone pre-merge journey test
code_assets.summary: End-to-end gate: clone, install from lockfiles, non-interactive setup, `graph mutate`, then query it back.
code_assets.description: The integration test validating the critical first-user path inside an isolated temp environment: clone the repository into a brand-new directory, install dependencies from lockfiles, run non-interactive setup, create graph data through `potpie graph mutate`, and verify the graph can then be queried. Helpers `_run`, `_run_json_cli`, `_unwrap_result`, `_isolated_env` (a clean `$CONTEXT_ENGINE_HOME`) and `_has_usable_rust_toolchain` keep it hermetic, with `_REPO_ROOT` resolved from `__file__` and `_CONTEXT_ENGINE_PROJECT = "potpie/context-engine"`. It lives at repo-root `tests/integration/`, not inside the engine package. Grep here when a release is blocked by the pre-merge journey gate or a fresh install regresses.

code_assets.name: potpie/pyproject.toml — the product distribution manifest
code_assets.summary: The root `potpie` package: three console scripts and the runtime dependency floor for the shipped CLI.
code_assets.description: Hatchling project file for `potpie` 2.0.0, the 'Potpie product distribution' (requires-python >=3.12,<3.15, Apache-2.0). It depends on `potpie-context-core==0.1.0` and `potpie-context-engine[all]==0.1.0` plus typer, rich, fastapi, uvicorn, mcp, pydantic-ai-slim, pydantic-settings, pyjwt, httpx, aiohttp and a `sentry-sdk>=2.61.1,<3.0.0` floor. `[project.scripts]` declares the three entrypoints — `potpie = potpie.cli.main:main`, `potpie-mcp = potpie.mcp.server:main` and `potpie-daemon = potpie.daemon.main:main` — which is the authoritative statement of what this package ships. This is the manifest Vanta CVE-remediation PRs bump. Grep here for a version floor, a console script name, or the boundaries of the three-package split.

code_assets.name: potpie/uv.lock — resolved dependency lock
code_assets.summary: The uv-resolved, hash-pinned dependency graph for the potpie workspace.
code_assets.description: Root lockfile produced by `uv lock` across the potpie uv workspace: every transitive package, exact version and wheel hash used by CI, by the pre-merge journey test's fresh-clone install, and by GitHub's dependency graph. Because Vanta and Dependabot read the lock rather than the floors in pyproject.toml, a CVE fix is only visible once this file is regenerated — and `.pre-commit-config.yaml` enforces freshness with the `uv-lock --check` hook, so a stale lock blocks the commit. Regenerate with `uv lock`; never hand-edit. Grep here to confirm the exact resolved version of a flagged transitive dependency.

code_assets.name: ontology.py — canonical entity/edge/record catalog
code_assets.summary: The single declarative catalog of every graph label, predicate and agent-facing record type.
code_assets.description: Canonical Potpie context-graph ontology: three spec-driven tables — ENTITY_TYPES (every label that can live in the graph, with identity class, key prefix, fact family, freshness TTL and classifier cues), EDGE_TYPES (every predicate that can ride a :RELATES_TO claim, grouped by category topology/ownership/people/timeline/memory/generic), and RECORD_TYPES (the context_record vocabulary joining record type to anchor entity, emitted predicate and reader include key). Adding an entity is one row in ENTITY_TYPES; adding a predicate is one row in EDGE_TYPES. Grep here for ONTOLOGY_VERSION, CANONICAL_EDGE_TYPES, is_canonical_entity_label, normalize_edge_name, allowed_pairs, scope=True, FACT_FAMILY_FRESHNESS_TTL_HOURS, or when you need to answer 'what labels/predicates exist' or 'why was my label downgraded'.

code_assets.name: graph_contract.py — versioned Graph V1.5 contract constants
code_assets.summary: One home for GRAPH_CONTRACT_VERSION, ONTOLOGY_VERSION, TruthClass, mutation-op partitions and entity/edge key helpers.
code_assets.description: Near-leaf module holding GRAPH_CONTRACT_VERSION = 'v1.5' and ONTOLOGY_VERSION = '2026-06-graph', plus TruthClass (authoritative_fact / source_observation / agent_claim / user_decision / preference / timeline_event / quality_finding) and its map onto the ranker's evidence-strength vocabulary. Also owns SemanticMutationOp partitioned into APPLICABLE_MUTATION_OPS / REVIEW_REQUIRED_OPS / DEFERRED_OPS, MutationRisk, SourceAuthority, EVIDENCE_REQUIRED_TRUTH_CLASSES, normalize_entity_key, make_claim_key and edge_identity_key (which folds `environment` in so an env-qualified edge never supersedes its counterpart in another environment). Imports nothing from ontology.py at module load — key helpers import lazily inside their bodies — to avoid an import cycle; look here for 'unsupported contract version' and is_supported_contract_version failures.

code_assets.name: identity.py — deterministic entity_key minting
code_assets.summary: Identity classes and the deterministic minting/validation of every entity_key in the graph.
code_assets.description: Defines IdentityClass (EXTERNAL_ID for PR/issue/commit/deploy events, SLUG_ALIAS for Service/Feature/Person/Team/Repository, CONTENT_HASH for Decision/Note/Document bodies), mint_entity_key (the LLM proposes a name, Potpie computes the key) and validate_entity_key (per-class grammar check). The slug grammar is lowercase letters, digits and hyphens with the class prefix separated by a single colon — `service:auth-svc`, `repo:potpie-ai/potpie`, `code:potpie:path/to/file.py`. Cross-source convergence ('auth service' vs 'auth-svc') runs through ALIAS_OF claim edges rather than a separate alias table. Search here for invalid entity key, key grammar, alias resolution, or all_identities().

code_assets.name: semantic_mutations.py — agent-facing write DTOs
code_assets.summary: The public semantic-mutation write contract agents emit instead of Cypher or EntityUpsert.
code_assets.description: Public DTOs for the agent-facing write tier above the internal backend-bound MutationBatch. Agents never see EntityUpsert / EdgeUpsert / Cypher — they emit semantic operations (link_entities, assert_claim, append_event, upsert_entity, invalidate_claim) which the validator risk-classifies and the lowerer turns into a MutationBatch. Canonical payload is batch-shaped {pot_id, operations: [...]}; a single-op alias {operation: '...'} is normalized at the parse boundary. GraphEntityRef carries key/type/name/properties/summary/description where `description` is the agent-authored retrieval card the local embedder indexes on write. Raises SemanticMutationParseError on structurally malformed payloads.

code_assets.name: semantic_mutation_validator.py — validation + risk policy
code_assets.summary: Rejects unsafe or ungrounded semantic mutations before they become structural writes.
code_assets.description: Domain-only validation of semantic mutation payloads: reads the ontology and contract constants, never a backend, so a payload can be checked without a store. Emits per-op structured issues (error / warning) plus a MutationRisk classification and a status of accepted / review_required / deferred / rejected; the batch decision is apply / review_required / rejected. A batch applies atomically — if any op cannot be auto-applied under the caller's approval flags the whole batch returns review_required and nothing is written. This is where 'evidence required for truth class', 'predicate not allowed between these labels' (allowed_pairs violations), unknown-label and missing-description findings originate.

code_assets.name: semantic_mutation_lowering.py — semantic ops → MutationBatch
code_assets.summary: The single bridge from agent-facing semantic ops to the backend-bound structural MutationBatch.
code_assets.description: The one place that turns SemanticMutation* operations into EntityUpsert / EdgeUpsert / InvalidationOp, stamping the full V1.5 claim metadata on every edge: truth, confidence, evidence/source_refs, the retrieval-card description, environment, valid_from/valid_to validity window, provenance, contract + ontology version, and the deterministic claim_key. Produces no EventRef for non-event writes — provenance flows through ProvenanceContext instead. If a claim lands in the graph missing truth, environment or claim_key, or if supersession picks the wrong counterpart, this lowerer is the file to read.

code_assets.name: graph_mutations.py — structural mutation + provenance types
code_assets.summary: Typed structural graph mutations (EntityUpsert, EdgeUpsert, EdgeDelete, InvalidationOp) and the first-class provenance record.
code_assets.description: Frozen dataclasses for the internal write vocabulary: EntityUpsert, EdgeUpsert, EdgeDelete, InvalidationOp and ProvenanceRef/ProvenanceContext. ProvenanceRef is the provenance contract every important fact carries so consumers can answer where did this come from, when was it observed, when was it last written, how confident, and who produced it — pot_id, source_event_id, prov_mutation_id (a per-apply UUID generated by apply_reconciliation_plan), source_system, source_kind, source_ref, event_occurred_at, graph_updated_at, valid_from/valid_to, confidence, created_by_agent, reconciliation_run_id and the actor_* fields (user id, surface, client name, auth method).

code_assets.name: ontology_classifier.py — signals → canonical labels
code_assets.summary: Deterministic classifier that pins flexible LLM entity output onto canonical ontology labels.
code_assets.description: Fully spec-driven classifier: reads its rule tables from ontology.py rather than hardcoding label strings, so teaching it a new entity means adding text_patterns / property_signatures to the entity spec. Three signal sources — edge-endpoint inference (EDGE_ENDPOINT_INFERRED_LABELS built from edge specs' source_inferred_labels / target_inferred_labels), property signatures (ENTITY_PROPERTY_SIGNATURES), and compiled text-pattern regexes (ENTITY_TEXT_CLASSIFIERS). Runs on both the reconciliation plan-enrichment path (canonical_label_inference) and the post-extraction pass over the canonical graph. When signals do not uniquely pick a label it returns nothing rather than guessing — a missing label is cheaper than a wrong one.

code_assets.name: coherence.py — import-time ontology invariants
code_assets.summary: Fails loud at import when the entity, edge, record, identity and reader vocabularies drift apart.
code_assets.description: Enforces that five vocabularies agree: ENTITY_TYPES, EDGE_TYPES, RECORD_TYPES, the identity registry (a view over ENTITY_TYPES), and the read-orchestrator's reader routing table. Drift symptoms are quiet — unsupported includes, silently dropped record types, predicates that never land claims — so cheap checks run at module import and fail startup fast, while assert_runtime_coherence() is called by the application bootstrap once readers are constructed to confirm actual readers match advertised READER_BACKED_INCLUDES. Raises OntologyCoherenceError naming the specific gap; the expected fix is always align the declaration, never relax the check.

code_assets.name: graph_workbench_ontology.py — executable Graph V2 catalog contract
code_assets.summary: Turns the view map, ontology catalogs and mutation-op partitions into the objects `graph catalog` and `graph describe` return.
code_assets.description: The static contract layer above the V1.5 data plane — the thing that makes `potpie graph catalog` self-describing so agents never need docs. Composes CONTEXT_INCLUDE_VALUES, GRAPH_VIEWS/GraphViewSpec, TRUTH_CLASSES, SOURCE_AUTHORITIES, STRONG_AUTHORITIES and the APPLICABLE/REVIEW_REQUIRED/DEFERRED mutation-op partitions into catalog and describe payloads. Reader behavior itself still lives in DefaultGraphService. Search here for graph catalog output shape, describe entity type, available views, which ops are applicable, or workbench contract version drift.

code_assets.name: workbench_service.py — Graph V2 envelope assembly
code_assets.summary: Shared assembly of every graph workbench response envelope — success, error and not-implemented.
code_assets.description: The largest module in context-core: builds the uniform envelopes the CLI, HTTP API and MCP surface all return for graph reads and writes. Exposes graph_success_envelope, graph_error_envelope, graph_not_implemented_envelope, new_graph_request_id, normalize_catalog_result and normalize_workbench_result, and threads validate_semantic_request → lower_semantic_request for the mutate path. Also stitches in graph history (GraphHistoryRequest/Result), the graph inbox (GraphInboxItem, TERMINAL_INBOX_STATUSES) and MutationRisk / EVIDENCE_REQUIRED_TRUTH_CLASSES so a rejected write comes back with a structured reason rather than a stack trace.

code_assets.name: event_playbooks.py — per-event extraction playbooks
code_assets.summary: Tells the reconciliation agent what a given (source, event_type, action) carries and what to extract from it.
code_assets.description: Each EventPlaybook maps a (source_system, event_type, action) combination to what the event typically carries, what should be extracted into the graph, and which tools tend to be useful; render_playbooks_section merges the playbooks for the events in a batch into the agent's run prompt so behavior is shaped by the events present rather than a static system prompt. Lookup falls back along a ladder — (source, type, action) → (source, type, '*') → (source, '*', '*') → ('*','*','*') → default — so narrow rules can be registered without enumerating every action variant. Playbook bodies are markdown skills loaded from the playbooks/ directory with YAML frontmatter stripped; a missing skill file yields an explicit 'stop and report this configuration error' body instead of silent degradation.

code_assets.name: repo_one_shot_ingestion.md — repo baseline ingestion playbook
code_assets.summary: The markdown skill body that drives one-shot repository baseline ingestion into the graph.
code_assets.description: Agent-facing skill markdown loaded by event_playbooks._load_skill_body and embedded directly into the reconciliation agent's prompt. Describes how to walk a freshly registered repository once and emit the baseline topology — repository, services, environments, datastores, dependencies, API contracts, features, ownership — as semantic mutations with grounded evidence. This is the file to edit when first-run `potpie` ingestion produces a thin or wrong baseline graph; it is the prose half of the repo-baseline behavior whose code half is the reconciliation agent.

code_assets.name: source_references.py — freshness, verification and source policy primitives
code_assets.summary: Normalized shape for pointers back to source systems, plus the freshness/verification/access state vocabularies.
code_assets.description: The context graph stores compact memory plus pointers back to source systems; this module owns that normalized shape. Defines SOURCE_POLICIES (references_only, summary, verify, snippets, full_if_needed), RESOLVE_MODES (fast, balanced, deep, verify), SOURCE_ACCESS_STATES (allowed, unknown, permission_denied, source_unreachable, missing), FRESHNESS_STATES (fresh, mostly_fresh, stale, needs_verification, source_unreachable, unknown), VERIFICATION_STATES and SOURCE_SYNC_STATES, plus SourceReferenceRecord and SourceFallback. Grep here when a resolve reports 'stale', 'needs_verification' or 'permission_denied' and you need to know what produced that state.

code_assets.name: graph_views.py — canonical named read views
code_assets.summary: Declares each `<subgraph>.<view>` read request and the V1 include it maps onto.
code_assets.description: A view is a named read request (`graph read --view topology.service`, `change.timeline`, `debug.prior_bugs`) mapping onto an internal reader family, declaring its inputs, which relations are inlined (the Retrieve axis), ranking inputs, and whether it is a bounded traversal (the Traverse axis). `backed` is derived, not hand-set: a view is backed iff its v1_include has a registered reader in READER_BACKED_INCLUDES, so unbacked views resolve to an honest not_implemented rather than silent zeros. An import-time check keeps every view's v1_include inside the advertised include vocabulary so views and the agent surface cannot drift.

code_assets.name: graph_quality.py — quality, drift and coverage policy
code_assets.summary: Computes per-resolve coverage, staleness and drift signals that back `potpie graph quality`.
code_assets.description: Owns the maintenance policy for agent-facing context: CoverageReport reports status complete / partial / empty with the available and missing evidence families for a resolve, and the module applies FACT_FAMILY_FRESHNESS_TTL_HOURS and SOURCE_OF_TRUTH_POLICIES to flag stale or contradicted claims. Also computes the supersession helpers (predicate_family_for_episodic_supersede, temporal_subject_key_for_edge, object_counterparty_uuid_for_edge) and emits the QualityIssue markers that record ontology downgrades. This is what `potpie graph quality` reads and what surfaces 'thin description', 'no evidence', 'orphan entity' and 'stale fact family' findings.

code_assets.name: context_events.py — ContextEvent, the ingestion unit
code_assets.summary: The normalized event every connector produces and the reconciliation agent consumes.
code_assets.description: Small but load-bearing: ContextEvent and EventRef are the single normalized shape a webhook, a manual submit, a repo scan or an integration poll all collapse into before batching. Carries pot_id, source_system, event_type, action, payload, occurred_at and the source reference used for provenance. Everything downstream — event admission, debounced batching, playbook lookup, agent prompting and MENTIONS provenance — keys off the (source_system, event_type, action) triple defined here.

code_assets.name: cypher.py — Position-B Cypher for the canonical graph
code_assets.summary: Direct Neo4j Cypher implementing the one-edge-per-claim substrate with bitemporal validity and supersession.
code_assets.description: Every claim is one :RELATES_TO edge between entities keyed by deterministic (group_id, entity_key). The edge carries the predicate as `name`, bitemporal validity (valid_at / invalid_at for event time, created_at / expired_at for system time), V1.5 claim metadata (truth, source_refs, claim_key), and the natural-language fact text the agent reads and the vector index embeds. The MERGE key includes source_ref so two distinct sources making the same claim land as two corroborating edges while a re-scan of the same source updates its edge idempotently in place. Validated end to end by pocs/position_b/poc.py including supersession, point-in-time queries, corroboration and native-vector semantic search. This is the file for 'why did my edge not supersede the old one' and for MERGE / randomUUID / dynamic SET e:Label questions.

code_assets.name: pydantic_deep_agent.py — the reconciliation agent
code_assets.summary: Single-agent ingestion loop that turns a batch of ContextEvents into graph mutations, checkpointed per tool call.
code_assets.description: Backed by pydantic-deep (upstream vstorm-co/pydantic-deepagents). Receives a batch of recently-arrived ContextEvents for a pot and runs to completion against a tool surface of read-only graph lookups (context_search, context_timeline), a fat mutation tool (apply_graph_mutations), event-completion control (mark_events_processed / mark_event_processed) and a terminal finish_batch tool. Merges the matching EventPlaybooks into its run prompt so behavior is event-shaped. Progress is checkpointed after every tool call through AgentCheckpointStorePort so a worker crash mid-run resumes on a follow-up dispatch. This is where ingestion hangs, runaway tool loops, empty-mutation runs and 'the agent never called finish_batch' are diagnosed.

code_assets.name: graph_service.py — DefaultGraphService, the data plane
code_assets.summary: The one door for catalog / read / search_entities / mutate over a GraphBackend.
code_assets.description: resolve and search run the one-read-trunk (ReadOrchestrator) over the backend's claim_query port. Graph Surface Lite adds catalog (derived from the ontology, view map and contract constants — no docs needed), read (maps a V2 view onto a V1 include, routes through the read trunk and stamps graph-contract metadata plus subgraph_versions), search_entities (projects claim rows into entity candidates for identity resolution before a write), and mutate (validate → risk-classify → lower → dry-run or apply). The V1 `record` write is rewired through the same semantic mutation path via record_to_semantic_request, so there is no private direct-lowering back door.

code_assets.name: process_batch.py — the ingestion worker entrypoint
code_assets.summary: Runs the reconciliation agent over one debounced batch and persists the outcome.
code_assets.description: Worker entrypoint: loads the batch, its events and any prior agent checkpoint, calls agent.run_batch, then marks events processed, drops the checkpoint on success, or marks the batch failed. Large batches split into chunks of CONTEXT_ENGINE_MAX_CHUNK_EVENTS (default 20) with the agent invoked once per chunk; each chunk gets a fresh pydantic-ai message history to bound prompt size while the shared graph context means a mutation from chunk N is visible to chunk N+1 via graph reads. Chunks run sequentially so mutation ordering is preserved. Emits work events for the live UI stream and wraps everything in a correlation_scope span.

code_assets.name: read_orchestrator.py — the single read trunk
code_assets.summary: Expands intent into include families, routes each to its reader, and assembles one ranked AgentEnvelope.
code_assets.description: One orchestrator is the entire read path and it does exactly four things: expand `intent` into include families via includes_for_request, route each include to its reader through the _ROUTING table, run each reader over the canonical claim store via ClaimQueryPort, and assemble one ranked AgentEnvelope. Includes that resolve to no reader are surfaced as unsupported_include with reason not_implemented rather than silently returning nothing — the anti-phantom-vocabulary rule. Small file, but every context_resolve and `potpie graph read` passes through it.

code_assets.name: timeline_reader.py — change/activity timeline reader
code_assets.summary: Surfaces Activity entities that touched a scope inside a window, ranked by recency and scope overlap.
code_assets.description: Takes scope plus a time window and returns the Activity entities that touched that scope, ranked by recency and scope overlap. Uses MENTIONS provenance so PR, ticket, deploy and alert activities all converge: any activity whose body mentioned the scope service has an outgoing MENTIONS edge back to it. Before MENTIONS existed, an Activity bound only to person:alice via PERFORMED was invisible to 'what activities touched service:auth-svc this week?'. This backs the change.timeline view and the recent-changes half of the potpie-change-timeline skill.

code_assets.name: prior_bugs.py — symptom-first bug and fix reader
code_assets.summary: Native-vector lookup of prior BugPattern/Fix claims by symptom signature and scope.
code_assets.description: Takes a free-text or structured symptom signature plus scope and runs a direct native-vector query through the claim-query port's fact_query over BugPattern-related claim edges, filtered to live edges and the agent's scope-or-broader. Ranks by verification × scope-overlap × recency × corroboration. Surfaces both worked fixes (RESOLVED claims) and attempted-failed fixes (ATTEMPTED_FIX_FAILED claims), the latter explicitly labeled so the agent does not repeat them, and hides narrower-scope bugs from broader-scope queries. This is the reader behind 'have we seen this stack trace before' and the potpie-debug-memory skill.

code_assets.name: infra_topology.py — topology and blast-radius reader
code_assets.summary: Bounded neighbourhood traversal over DEFINED_IN / DEPLOYED_TO / DEPENDS_ON / USES / HOSTED_ON / OWNED_BY claims.
code_assets.description: Takes a scope (service, environment or file) and does a bounded neighbourhood traversal over topology-predicate claim edges — DEFINED_IN, DEPLOYED_TO, DEPENDS_ON, USES, HOSTED_ON, OWNED_BY, PROVIDES, IMPLEMENTED_IN — environment-filtered via the `environment` edge property and supporting as_of via the bitemporal predicate. Supports blast radius through incoming DEPENDS_ON traversal with a depth bound. When a free-text query is supplied, discovered rows are scored with semantic_similarity so ranking is query-sensitive while the traversal itself stays query-free. Answers 'what env runs auth-svc' and 'what breaks if this service goes down'.

code_assets.name: ranking.py — the uniform retrieval ranker
code_assets.summary: Scores every candidate claim by strength × recency × scope_overlap × corroboration × semantic_similarity.
code_assets.description: One formula serves every reader: readers extract the per-factor inputs (which are use-case specific) and RankingService applies the uniform product with a coverage-quality downweight. Semantic similarity carries the highest default weight because with embed-on-write plus ANN it is the primary recall signal. The module is deliberately I/O-free — callers build Candidate objects from graph reads and get back RankedItem objects with the full score breakdown attached so readers can explain rankings to the agent and so 'higher-strength wins, every time, deterministically' is testable. Grep here when results are ordered surprisingly or when tuning retrieval weights.

code_assets.name: in_memory_backend.py — embedded/JSON-persisted graph backend
code_assets.summary: Zero-dependency graph backend that makes `pip install potpie` enough to have a working context graph.
code_assets.description: Full GraphBackend implementation over in-process dictionaries with JSON persistence, reproducing the Position-B claim substrate — bitemporal validity, supersession, claim_key identity and vector search over locally embedded fact text — without Neo4j, FalkorDB or Docker. This is why embeddings must be deterministic across processes (see local_embedder's stable digest hashing): the persisted JSON is reloaded by a different process and vectors must still match. Used by the default local profile, the test suite and the benchmark harness.

code_assets.name: neo4j_backend.py — Neo4j GraphBackend binding
code_assets.summary: Binds the GraphBackend port to a Neo4j driver, delegating all mutation Cypher to cypher.py.
code_assets.description: Thin backend that owns driver lifecycle, session/transaction management, index creation and pot reset against Neo4j, and delegates the actual claim reads/writes to the shared cypher.py functions so bitemporal and supersession logic lives in exactly one place. This is the production backend for hosted pots (the neo4j-cluster / neo4j-helm workloads in potpie-k8s-deployments). Read here for connection URI/auth configuration, 'ServiceUnavailable', constraint/index bootstrap and vector-index creation failures.

code_assets.name: local_embedder.py — no-API-key local embedder
code_assets.summary: Feature-hashing embedder that makes retrieval work with no API key and no external embedding service.
code_assets.description: The Trigger Model non-negotiable is that retrieval must work offline on the user's machine, so this is the default OSS embedder: text is tokenized into words and character n-grams, each feature hashed via a stable digest (identical embeddings across processes — required for the JSON-persisted embedded backend) into a fixed-dimension accumulator with a signed contribution, then L2-normalized. It beats the old Jaccard stub because it scores in continuous vector space so near-misses rank above noise, and character n-grams catch morphological variants (retry / retries / retrying share trigrams) and typos. build_embedder reads CONTEXT_ENGINE_EMBEDDER first, then the local setup config; `potpie setup` can persist sentence-transformers for a stronger local model.

code_assets.name: otel.py — OpenTelemetry observability adapter
code_assets.summary: The only module importing opentelemetry; exports OTLP spans to the collector, provider-aware and fail-open.
code_assets.description: Implements ObservabilityPort over OTLP to a collector (Tempo / Prometheus) and is the single opentelemetry import in the codebase, which is what keeps the backend swappable. Provider-aware: when a parent TracerProvider already exists (running inside the Potpie Celery worker where Logfire instruments pydantic-ai) it attaches an extra OTLP BatchSpanProcessor to the existing provider and never calls set_tracer_provider, so model and tool spans nest under our event spans automatically; standalone HTTP/CLI/MCP gets a fresh provider. Configured entirely through standard OTEL_* env such as OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT. If the observability extra is not installed or any setup step fails it degrades to a silent no-op — observability never fails the process.

code_assets.name: redis_publisher.py — Redis Streams event publisher
code_assets.summary: Publishes per-event work timelines and per-pot status deltas onto Redis Streams for the live UI.
code_assets.description: Implements EventStreamPublisherPort with two stream key schemes: `events:activity:{event_id}` for the per-event work-event timeline (replayed in full when a user opens the side-panel detail, then tailed live) and `events:status:{pot_id}` for coarse lifecycle deltas on every event in a pot (tailed by the list view so row indicators update without polling). Mirrors the chat RedisStreamManager's TTL, max-len and wait behaviour so operators have one mental model, without importing it, keeping the context-engine package self-contained. This is the server half of potpie-ui's EventStreamService NDJSON stream.

code_assets.name: connector.py — GitHub source connector
code_assets.summary: Single point of contact for everything GitHub: reads, reference resolution, webhook parsing and agent tools.
code_assets.description: Bundles four GitHub-shaped surfaces behind one class — read access to PRs and issues via api_client, reference resolution via fetch(), webhook signature verification and parsing via normalize_webhook() (called from adapters/inbound/http/webhooks/integrations/github.py), and agent tool bindings via build_github_agent_tools. The application layer never imports anything in this module. Deterministic PR-merge plan compilation (propose_plan) was deliberately removed: webhooks now produce raw ContextEvents and the deterministic activity layer plus the LLM reconciliation agent turn them into :RELATES_TO claims. Look here for HMAC signature mismatch and unparsed webhook payload issues.

code_assets.name: api_client.py — PyGithub-backed GitHub read port
code_assets.summary: GitHubReadPort implementation over PyGithub for PRs, issues, commits, diffs and file contents.
code_assets.description: Defines GitHubReadPort and its PyGithubSourceControl implementation — the only place PyGithub is imported. Handles app/installation and PAT auth, rate-limit handling, and fetching pull requests, issues, review comments, commit lists and file contents used both by reference resolution and by the agent's GitHub tools. Grep here for 403 rate limit exceeded, 404 on private repos, bad credentials, and installation-token refresh.

code_assets.name: router.py — context graph HTTP API v1
code_assets.summary: The FastAPI surface for pots, sources, events, graph reads and graph mutations that potpie-ui talks to.
code_assets.description: Largest inbound adapter: exposes the /api/v1/context endpoints for pot CRUD and membership, source registration and refresh, ingestion event listing and detail, event activity and pot status streams, graph catalog/read/search-entities/mutate, and ingestion configuration. Serves both the standalone context-engine service and the host-injected deployment, with dependencies resolved through get_container_or_503 / get_db. This is the exact contract potpie-ui's services/PotService.ts and EventStreamService.ts are written against — check here when a UI call 404s or the response shape drifts.

code_assets.name: ingestion_submission_service.py — event admission and batching front door
code_assets.summary: Accepts an IngestionSubmissionRequest, admits or dedupes the event, and attaches it to a debounced batch.
code_assets.description: Every path into the graph — webhook, manual CLI submit, source refresh, UI re-ingest — funnels through this service. It validates the submission, applies event admission rules (dedupe by source event id, pot scope check, ingestion-kind routing), persists the ingestion event, and attaches it to the open debounce window so bursty webhooks collapse into one agent run. Emits the initial status stream delta that lights up the pot events console. Search here for duplicate event ignored, event rejected, batch already closed, and 'my event is stuck in queued'.

code_assets.name: nudge_service.py — local-embedder-only nudge policy
code_assets.summary: Owns every decision about what to read and whether to prompt a write when a harness hook fires.
code_assets.description: Backs `potpie graph nudge`: given a harness hook event (session start, pre-tool-use, post-tool-use, test_failed, test_passed) it decides whether the graph has relevant context worth injecting and whether the session produced a durable learning worth writing back. Uses only the local embedder — no model call — so nudges are free and offline. All trigger policy lives here rather than in the hook adapter, which is deliberately model-free field-forwarding. This is the file behind 'Potpie injected irrelevant context' and 'Potpie never nudged me to record anything'.

code_assets.name: main.py — the potpie CLI spine
code_assets.summary: Assembles every command group into one Typer app bound to a HostShell — the `potpie` console entrypoint.
code_assets.description: The architecture's single spine: assembles the per-group sub-apps (auth, bootstrap, cloud, daemon, graph, ledger, pots, query, service, skills, telemetry, ui) into one Typer app and binds them to a HostShell so every command routes CLI → HostShell → service(s) → ports. This is the `potpie` console_script declared in [project.scripts]; the in-process HostShell is the only composition root for the agent surface. Run `potpie --help` or `python -m potpie.cli.main --help`. Add a new command group here.

code_assets.name: graph.py — the `potpie graph` command group
code_assets.summary: The largest CLI module: catalog, read, search-entities, propose, commit, quality, inbox, nudge, status.
code_assets.description: Implements the whole graph workbench surface agents drive — `potpie graph catalog` (discover the contract), `graph read --view` (named views), `graph search-entities` (identity resolution before a write), `graph propose` / `graph commit --verify` (validated plans), `graph quality`, `graph inbox`, `graph nudge` and `graph status`. CLI code never touches a store directly; everything goes through capability ports, and unbuilt projections (semantic / inspection / analytics / snapshot on profiles that lack them) surface as the structured not-implemented contract rather than a crash. Emits JSON envelopes via graph_success_envelope / graph_error_envelope with exit codes EXIT_VALIDATION and EXIT_UNAVAILABLE.

code_assets.name: pots.py — the `potpie pot` and source command group
code_assets.summary: Pot creation, listing, selection and source registration bound to PotManagementService.
code_assets.description: Implements `potpie pot list/create/use/show` and `potpie source list/add/refresh/remove`, resolving which pot a repository is bound to via repo_identity_key / resolve_repo_location and the pot-scope helpers (resolve_pot_scope, repo_effective_pot_info, repo_pot_candidates). Emits onboarding telemetry through capture_project_binding_event. This is where 'no pot selected', 'this repo is not bound to a pot', ambiguous pot resolution and empty-pot warnings originate — the first commands a new user hits after `potpie setup`.

code_assets.name: bootstrap.py — setup / status / doctor / config
code_assets.summary: The idempotent first-run sequence plus the cheap aggregate health commands.
code_assets.description: `potpie setup` runs the documented idempotent first-run sequence against the host services, proving the journey shape end to end; `potpie status` is the cheap aggregate composed from all three services via context_status; `potpie doctor` diagnoses install, auth, backend and pot-binding problems; `potpie config` reads and writes local configuration. Returns EXIT_DEGRADED when the system works but something is off. This is the file behind every 'potpie doctor says X' question and the first thing to read for local dev setup failures.

code_assets.name: potpie_nudge.py — harness hook adapter
code_assets.summary: The thin, model-free hook forwarder that maps a Claude Code / Codex / Cursor hook event to `potpie graph nudge`.
code_assets.description: A harness fires a hook event; this adapter reads the payload from stdin, mechanically maps it to a single `potpie graph nudge` call, and injects the returned context or instruction back into the session. It owns no trigger policy and makes no model call — every decision about what to read, whether it is relevant, and whether to prompt a write lives in nudge_service behind the CLI. Its only real logic is field-forwarding plus the mechanical event-name mapping the harness taxonomy forces (one PostToolUse(Bash) event must become either test_failed or test_passed). Fail-safe by construction: any internal error, missing `potpie` binary or unparseable payload exits 0 with no output so a hook problem can never block or corrupt the user's session. Set POTPIE_HOOK_DEBUG=1 for stderr diagnostics.

code_assets.name: server.py — the MCP four-tool context surface
code_assets.summary: FastMCP server exposing context_resolve / context_search / context_record / context_status in-process.
code_assets.description: The MCP binding of AgentContextPort — the same port the CLI and HTTP surfaces use. Runs the engine in-process via build_host_shell rather than as an HTTP client to a managed API, so a local agent (claude-code, cursor, copilot) talks straight to the local context graph through the same services the CLI uses. Maps context_resolve → host.agent_context.resolve, context_search → search, context_record → record, context_status → status. Read here for MCP stdio registration, tool schema drift, and 'the MCP tools return empty but the CLI works'.

code_assets.name: py_graph.py — tree-sitter repo symbol graph builder
code_assets.summary: Builds a networkx MultiDiGraph of definitions and references across a repo using tree-sitter tags.
code_assets.description: create_graph(repo_dir) walks a checkout and, per file, picks a language via grep_ast.filename_to_lang and tree_sitter_language_pack, runs tag queries with QueryCursor, and records Tag(rel_fname, fname, line, end_line, name, kind, type, byte_start, byte_end) rows into `defines` and `references` maps, which become a networkx MultiDiGraph of code structure. Falls back to pygments guess_lexer_for_filename when tree-sitter has no grammar, tolerating ClassNotFound. This is the code-structure parser behind repo ingestion and the code-search tools; read it for unsupported language, missing grammar, and huge-repo parse slowness.

code_assets.name: integrations_service.py — third-party integration lifecycle
code_assets.summary: OAuth connect/refresh/disconnect and status for Sentry, Linear, Jira and Confluence.
code_assets.description: Application service coordinating every third-party integration: SentryOAuthV2, LinearOAuth, JiraOAuth and ConfluenceOAuth flows, token storage and refresh, per-org integration records, and the status payloads (SentryIntegrationStatus, LinearIntegrationStatus, JiraIntegrationStatus, ConfluenceIntegrationStatus) the settings UI renders. Also owns IntegrationCreateRequest / IntegrationUpdateRequest / IntegrationListResponse and the IntegrationType and IntegrationStatus enums. This is where 'integration shows disconnected after token expiry', invalid state parameter, and scope-mismatch errors are handled.

code_assets.name: PotService.ts — the pot API client
code_assets.summary: Axios client for every pot, source, member, invitation, event, ingestion and graph endpoint, with demo-pot interception.
code_assets.description: The single frontend gateway to the context-engine HTTP API: listPots, pot CRUD, source registration and refresh, member and invitation flows (PotRole owner/user, PotPendingInvitation with token for accept/decline), ingestion event listing and detail, ingestion config, the pipeline snapshot, graph overview and context queries. Every call first checks the demo interceptors from lib/mock/demoPots (isDemoPotId, isDemoEventId, isDemoInviteToken, getDemo*) so the three seeded demo pots resolve without a backend. Base URL comes from NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL and auth headers from app/utils/headers.util. Start here when a pots screen shows stale or missing data.

code_assets.name: EventStreamService.ts — NDJSON activity/status stream client

code_assets.name: PotGraphCanvas.tsx — force-directed pot graph renderer
code_assets.summary: Neo4j-browser-style SVG force graph with a spanning-forest backbone that keeps a dense pot graph from becoming a hairball.
code_assets.description: Renders the pot ontology as plain SVG driven by d3-force: flat category-coloured discs with a darker rim, captions wrapped inside the disc, relationship-type labels along edges, arrowheads at the target end, and a transparent background so the page's pot-dots texture shows through. Layout is hub-and-ring via a spanning-forest backbone — a pot graph is dense (hundreds of nodes, ~6 edges each) so every node picks ONE parent (its nearest-bigger neighbour, not the biggest, which would collapse the forest into a single star) and only that link is stiff with a rest length equal to the hub's ring radius; every other edge renders but keeps ~zero strength. React owns structure (which nodes and edges exist, mounted once) while ticks, pan/zoom, selection emphasis, fades and label visibility are written straight into the DOM via refs, because routing a click through React would reconcile ~1.3k memoised components at once. Read this for graph jank, hairball layout, and selection lag.

code_assets.name: __init__.py — the frozen observability public contract
code_assets.summary: Three-function frozen API — get_logger, configure, log_context — over stdlib logging with pluggable sinks.
code_assets.description: FROZEN PUBLIC CONTRACT: only get_logger(name) → StructuredLogger, configure(config) → None (idempotent composition root), and log_context(**fields) context manager for correlation-id propagation are behavioral API; the config and Sink protocol are re-exported as data/typing contracts. Design is stdlib logging at the core with consumers staying ambient and backends (loguru, Sentry, logfire) plugging in through the single Sink seam, with no app.* imports anywhere so the package stays liftable into any Python service. Documented edge case EC1: stdlib loggers reject arbitrary kwargs, so StructuredLogger maps **fields onto record.obs_fields to keep the codebase's loguru-style logger.info('msg', key=val) working as structured fields rather than f-string blobs.
